questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Lean the same way the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. Sit as close to the operator as you can without crowding them. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if you can.
Stay seated and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before you hit it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What should you see when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A mirror may show your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and to the side is what matters most.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycle riders and other drivers?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers. Riders should be extra careful when approaching and crossing intersections.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with activities to slow their drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never let an impaired person ride a motorcycle. Instead, arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with other activities, and get other friends to help stop them from riding until they are sober.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle-car crashes are caused by drivers failing to yield to riders?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: Over half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because the driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the rider.

questions.question: What lane position should riders generally use?

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions often to avoid boredom.
Choose the lane position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose the lane position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. Choose the lane position that gives you the most space and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Gradually brake.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. It will make the problem worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Lean your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this may also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. When is this area safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: It is never safe.
It is usually safe, but not when the road is wet.
It is usually safe, but not when it is sunny.
It is always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is usually safe, but not when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips onto the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for safe riding. The oily strip is usually only about two feet wide. You can often ride around it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the car ahead as closely as possible.
Do not look ahead. Focus only on your controls.
Let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To lower crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. If you need to stop fast, use both brakes. Practice using both brakes every time so it becomes a habit.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can block your side view.
They let you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
They are dangerous to wear.
You do not have to wear them if you think they block your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit their vision. This is not true. Any approved helmet gives you enough side vision for safe riding.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up on the throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and stay on a straight path as you slow down. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake of the good tire only, if you know which one it is.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. You cannot speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake softer than usual to protect the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight from a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: When are safe motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When other motorists can see them.
When they ride faster than other vehicles.
When they are on the side of the road.
When they ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When other motorists can see them.
questions.explanation: Safe motorcyclists know that being seen by other drivers keeps them safest. Use your headlight, brake light, and turn signals. Position yourself in the lane to increase visibility.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or on the sides of your helmet makes you easier to see. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to stay balanced.
Keep your speed steady to improve traction.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads when you can. If you must go through one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: The body removes about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their system?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: When riding at night instead of during the day, a motorcycle operator should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Leave more space between their motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use their high beam whenever possible.
Tailgate other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower and leave more space between you and other vehicles. Use the headlights ahead of you to see farther. Never tailgate. Stay flexible with your lane position.
